title: L0178
description: Output of an L0178 program — the normalized Data API job plus steering warnings. This is NOT the deliverable; the developer-facing cookbook recipe is produced by get_spec. Atomic dialect (not a composition upstream).

endpoint.description: The Learnosity endpoint path this job targets, minus the {LTS_VERSION} prefix (e.g. "itembank/items"). Selected by the block function. Use this on the wire, never the block keyword.

action.description: The Data API action, sent in the request body. Every call is a POST regardless — the Data API is not REST. Note the verb does not imply read-vs-write: some get operations start jobs that mutate.

paged.description: True when this operation returns meta.next and must be paged. When true, a paging policy is required for the design to be complete.

paging_end.description: How a paged read knows it is finished, per endpoint. "next-absent": meta.next disappears at exhaustion (itembank/*). "empty-page": meta.next is ALWAYS present — it is a long-poll cursor — so the loop ends on a page with zero records (sessions/*). There is no correct universal loop; each family's rule is a bug in the other. Present only on paged blocks.

async.description: True when this operation returns { data: { job_reference } } instead of a result, to be polled with the jobs endpoint. Disjoint from paged — an operation returns one or the other, never both.

poll_with.description: Where an asynchronous operation is redeemed. Present only when async is true. Carries the channel (always the jobs endpoint with action get) and job_reference_at — where the reference sits in THIS endpoint's response, which differs per endpoint: some return data[0].job_reference, others data.job_reference, and both are real. Reading the wrong one yields undefined and a poll that never finds its job.

writes.description: True when the operation persists. Not the same as action !== "get" — some get operations start jobs that mutate.

write_semantics.description: How a write treats what is already there, measured per (endpoint, action) and NEVER inferred from the verb. "replace": anything omitted from the payload is cleared. "merge": the sent values are added to what is there. ABSENT means it has not been established for that operation — only the tag-assignment endpoints have been measured — and absence must be read as unknown, not as safe.

paging.description: The declared paging policy. DESIGN INTENT — it has no Learnosity path and is never sent in a request. "exhaustive" follows meta.next to the end; "single-page" deliberately takes one page and accepts an incomplete result.

request.description: The job's request fields, keyed by their kebab DSL names. Read the wire path for each from `paths` — do not derive it from the key name.

paths.description: Every request field this job sets, mapped to its exact Learnosity path (e.g. "include-items" -> "include.items", "item-pool-id" -> "item_pool_id"). The recipe must read paths from here rather than deriving them from kebab key names, which are ambiguous about nesting. A key absent here was dropped and must not appear in the recipe.

complete.description: True when the job has no unfilled holes (an operation is selected, and a paged operation declares how far it reads).

warnings.description: Steering hints: holes first (missing operation, undeclared paging policy), then validity warnings for input that was rejected or dropped, then specificity advisories. The client refines the job until these clear.
